lines.caption: What if your whole backend… was one TypeScript class?
No tricks. Watch it turn into a database, an API, a typed client and security rules.
Hi, I'm Ray! Welcome to Learn Rayfin with Ray.
Today: what Rayfin is, how one class becomes a whole backend, and how it ships to Microsoft Fabric. Let’s dive in!
A backend usually means a database, migrations, APIs, sign-in, hosting and security rules… all kept in sync by hand.
Rayfin is a backend platform for TypeScript developers. You describe your data once, in TypeScript, and Rayfin generates the backend and runs it on Microsoft Fabric.
Rayfin's data starts with an entity: a TypeScript class with decorators.
The entity decorator marks the class as data that Rayfin stores and serves.
Each field gets a decorator too: text with a maximum length, a decimal for the amount, and a date for when you spent it.
And the role decorator decides who can touch it. Its policy says: signed-in people only see their own expenses.
Time for a deep dive! Let's see what Rayfin makes from that one class.
A database table to store your expenses, and REST and GraphQL APIs to read and write them.
A type-safe client, so your editor knows every field. Row-level security, so people only see their own rows. Even form validation!
No SQL to write, no schema file, and no API contract to keep in sync by hand. Just one class.
Then one command, rayfin up, deploys it all to Microsoft Fabric, as a Fabric app.
Fabric hosts the database, the APIs, sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID, and your app's frontend, inside your organization's tenant. You didn't lift a fin.
Here's the same idea in Fabricator. Describe your app in plain English…
…and Fabricator's agent writes the entity for you. See? The entity decorator, and a role with its policy.
Blueprint draws it as a diagram: every field, its type, and who can see it.
And Fabricator runs rayfin up for you, then redeploys after every successful chat turn.
Pop quiz! Which part of an entity decides who can see each row?
A, the entity decorator. B, the text decorator. Or C, the role decorator, with its policy.
Pause the video, and guess…
It's C! The role decorator's policy keeps each person's rows their own.

lines.said: Let's recap. An entity is a TypeScript class with decorators. From it, Rayfin makes your table, API's, typed client and security. And rayfin up ships it all to Microsoft Fabric.
